text_run.content: A grouping search allows <include target="milvus">Milvus</include><include target="zilliz">Zilliz Cloud</include> to group the search results by the values in a specified field to aggregate data at a higher level. For example, you can use a basic ANN search to find books similar to the one at hand, but you can use a grouping search to find the book categories that may involve the topics discussed in that book. This topic describes how to use Grouping Search along with key considerations.
When entities in the search results share the same value in a scalar field, this indicates that they are similar in a particular attribute, which may negatively impact the search results.
Assume a collection stores multiple documents (denoted by
). To retain as much semantic information as possible when converting documents into vectors, each document is split into smaller, manageable paragraphs (or
) and stored as separate entities. Even though the document is divided into smaller sections, users are often still interested in identifying which documents are most relevant to their needs.

When performing an Approximate Nearest Neighbor (ANN) search on such a collection, the search results may include several paragraphs from the same document, potentially causing other documents to be overlooked, which may not align with the intended use case.
